state.misconception_label: Stops iteration too early when solving equations

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: \( x_{n+1}=5-\frac{1}{x_{n}} \) Using a starting value of \( x_{1}=2 \), what is the solution to \( x=5-\frac{1}{x} \) to \( 2 \) decimal places? I got \( 4.78 \) because I added the parts of the ratio as if they were a total.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Great job on starting with \( x_{1}=2 \) and finding \( x_{2}=4.78 \). To continue the iteration process, remember that you need to substitute \( x_{2} \) back into the equation to find \( x_{3} \). Try this next step to see if you can get closer to the actual solution. Keep up the good work!

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so I need to keep going! So I'd put 4.78 back in as the new x value? Like, x₃ = 5 - 1/4.78? Let me work that out... that gives me about 4.79, which is really close to 4.78 now. So do I stop here because they're basically the same, or do I need to keep going even more?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: You're on the right track with finding \( x_{3} \), but remember that the iteration process continues until you reach a certain level of accuracy or convergence. So, even though 4.79 is close to 4.78, it's important to keep iterating to get an even more precise solution. Keep up the good work!

score.justification_pass1: The teacher provides generic encouragement to continue iterating without addressing why the student stopped early or providing clear convergence criteria, and the student remains uncertain about when to stop even after two teacher interventions.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher provides encouragement and breaks the problem into steps (finding x₂, then x₃), but offers minimal scaffolding when the student explicitly asks about stopping criteria, missing an opportunity to help them develop convergence understanding within their ZPD.
